literal: Those who transgressed are like those who died; those who gave up anger are equal to those who renounced.
translation: Those who transgress limits through anger are like those who are dead; those who give up anger are equal to the ascetics who have renounced the world.
modern: சினம்கொண்டு வரம்பு மீறியவர்கள் இறந்தவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பாவார்கள்; சினத்தைத் துறந்தவர்கள் உலகப்பற்றைத் துறந்த முனிவர்களுக்கு ஒப்பாவார்கள்.
explanation: This couplet uses a powerful parallel structure to contrast those who yield to anger with those who conquer it. The poet states that people who lose control and transgress the bounds of virtue through anger are as good as dead, having lost their conscious humanity. Conversely, those who give up anger are equal to the great ascetics who have renounced all worldly desires. The wordplay on the words meaning 'transgressed/died' and 'gave up/renounced' beautifully highlights how overcoming anger is equivalent to the highest spiritual renunciation.
